authorisation: 2026-10-04 research-program mission, section 9.1 Priority 2: 'Native-resolution evaluation of existing checkpoints'
class: EXPLORATORY EXPERIMENT (Phase B additional control on frozen checkpoints; never merged into the reproduction columns)
question: Does the test-time input scale explain the test-split surplus of our reproduction over the paper (normal +5.22, DFSC +4.25 mSA) while validation agrees with the paper?
hypothesis: H4: the paper's numbers were produced with IR evaluated at native 640x512, whereas our Phase A evaluations rescale IR to 1000x800 (GlobalTrack 1333x800 rule).
controlled_variable: test-time rescale target only: (1333, 800) -> 1000x800 [reference = existing Phase A evaluations] vs (640, 512) -> 640x512, no resize [new]
held_fixed: checkpoints (final epoch, no selection), tracker, metric implementation, frozen split manifests, start frames, scoring code, git commit of the evaluator
run_policy: all four run regardless of intermediate results; no early stopping on outcomes; a failed run is re-run once from scratch (evaluate.py has no sequence resume)
dataset: Anti-UAV IR (arXiv:2101.08466 Protocol II), frozen manifests val a688bf92c46dfc52..., test 1fc351c74f4b29cc...
metric: mSA (paper Eq. 1, frames >= official start frame), plus per-attribute mSA (OV, OC, FM, SV, LI, TC*, LR)
prediction_if_H4_true: native-scale mSA reproduces the paper on BOTH splits: test drops by roughly the surplus (4-5 pt), concentrated on LR / LI / FM / SV, while validation stays within 1 pt of the paper

decision_rule.SUPPORTED: for both models: |native_val - paper_val| <= 1.0 AND |native_test - paper_test| <= 1.0
decision_rule.PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED: for both models: |native_val - paper_val| <= 1.0 AND (reference_test - native_test) >= 0.5 * (reference_test - paper_test)
decision_rule.NOT_SUPPORTED_VAL_BREAKS: for at least one model: native_val < paper_val - 1.0 (native evaluation no longer reproduces the paper's validation, so it cannot reconcile both splits)
decision_rule.NOT_SUPPORTED_INSENSITIVE: for both models: |native - reference| <= 1.0 on both splits

descriptive_outputs: delta (native - reference) per model x split x attribute; val/test asymmetry (delta_test - delta_val); fps
known_confound: eval-only probe: the checkpoints were trained at the 1000x800 scale, so native evaluation mixes 'lower resolution' with 'train/test scale mismatch'. A symmetric drop on both splits is most likely the mismatch and says little about the paper. Decisive follow-up only if a pronounced asymmetry appears (delta_test - delta_val <= -2 pt for both models): train at native scale and evaluate at native scale (separate pre-registration).
test_exposure: two additional TEST evaluations of already-evaluated frozen checkpoints, ledger-flagged phase B / variant test_scale_640x512; nothing is selected with them
disclosure: Before this registration a 1-sequence code smoke test was run on VAL sequence 20190925_101846_1_4 (normal_ir): SA 72.24 at the reference scale (reproduces the historical predictions, max score diff 2.8e-5) and 64.50 at native scale. No full-split result was seen before the rule above was fixed.
hardware: local OMEN RTX 5050 Laptop (remote HPC access unavailable on 2026-10-04)
